notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Ecclesiastes 7 this time, because the research tools stopped working before I could get anything back.

My first attempt to open the commentary pages (Enduring Word, BibleHub, StudyLight's copy of Wesley's notes, and the NET Bible notes) failed. A second try with a plain search also failed. Both times the tool reported that I had no more web calls left for this turn, so I never read a single source page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. With no pages read, I have nothing I can honestly give you. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, not from the listed sites, and the URLs couldn't be checked.

If you ask again in a new turn, the tools may be available. I would then:

1. **Read these first:** enduringword.com on Ecclesiastes 7, the BibleHub verse pages (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Matthew Henry, Barnes), Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu or studylight.org, and preceptaustin.org.
2. **Look for differences between traditions on the verses most likely to show them:**
   - v. 16 ("overly righteous") and v. 20 (no one is without sin): Reformed, Lutheran and Wesleyan/Holiness views differ on sin and on whether Christians can be made fully holy in this life.
   - v. 26 and v. 28 (the "snare" woman and "not one woman").
   - v. 29 (God made people upright): views on original sin.
3. **Add other views where the sites cover them:** NET Bible translation notes (e.g., on vv. 7, 12 and 27–28), bibleodyssey.org, Catholic and Orthodox readings on newadvent.org and oca.org, and gotquestions.org pages on these verses.

If the tools stay limited, I could also do one section at a time (say vv. 1–14, then 15–29) to use fewer calls.
